post.description: Generates an authentication token to be used with API calls. Once generated, token is valid for 48 hours and time-to-live is extended to 48 hours each time it is used up to 30 days. Tokens are expected to be sent with every API requests via **`Authorization`** request header.

get.description:
Obtains historical positions of requested trackers. #### Query-String Parameters: __Parameter__ | __Description__ --- | --- trackerId | __`_id`__ of the tracker that the you run this request for floorPlanId | List of __`_id`__ of the floor plan(s) that the you run this request for ts.since | This is the timestamp for the __start__ of the specified time window. _Default: Epoch._ ts.until | This is the timestamp for the __end__ of the specified time window. _Default: Current timestamp._ _limit | This specifies the maximum number of records to return. _Default: 1000_ _sortOrder | This specifies timestamp sort order. _Default: DESC_ #### Response Attributes: Response is a JSON array consist of objects with following attributes. __Attribute__ | | __Description__ --- | --- | --- ts | | Timestamp of the position (UTC) floorPlanId | | __`_id`__ of the position's floor plan coordinates | x | X coordinate of the position according the most left of the floor plan (meters) | y | Y coordinate of the position according to the bottom of the floor plan (meters)
__NOTE:__ The number of records returned is limited by the __`_limit`__ query parameter therefore the result set might not include all the records within the requested time window. In cases where your selection has more results than the limit, **`X-TRIO-Result-Set-Too-Large`** response header will be returned as **`true`** and you are expected to make a follow up request for the remaing items with an ensuing time window.

For example, assume a request to this endpoint with query parameters: __`_sortOrder=DESC`__, __`_limit=5000`__, __`ts.since=2017-01-01T00:00:00Z`__ and __`ts.until=2017-03-01T00:00:00Z`__ (an interval of 2 months) returns a result set of _5000_ items with __`ts`__ attriubutes ranging from __`2017-03-01T00:00:00Z`__ to __`2017-02-15T00:00:00Z`__ (a time interal of 15 days) indicates, the result set does not include all the records within the requested 2 months time interval and as per the limit, only the _first_ 5000 records in descending order that covers a 15 days time period is returned. Therefore a follow up request can be made with query parameters __`_sortOrder=DESC`__, __`_limit=5000`__, __`ts.since=2017-01-01T00:00:00Z`__ and __`ts.until=2017-02-15T00:00:00Z`__ (an interval of 45 days for the remaining time period). This type of follow up requests can be made until the whole time window is covered.

Obtains latest positions of trackers. #### Query-String Parameters: __Parameter__ | __Description__ --- | --- trackerId | List of __`_id`__ of the trackers that you run this request for. _If omited returns latest positions of all trackers (Pagination rules apply)_ _page | The starting list page offset, used for pagination. For example, if __`_perPage`__ is **`20`** and __`_page`__ is **`5`**, results from 80th to 100th is returned. _Default: 1_ _perPage | This specifies the maximum number of records to return. _Default: 20_ _sortBy | This specifies column to sort the results by. _sortOrder | This specifies sort order. _Default: DESC_ _pull | ... #### Response Attributes: Response is a JSON array consist of objects with following attributes. __Attribute__ | | __Description__ --- | --- | --- ts | | Timestamp of the position (UTC) tracker | _id | __`_id`__ of the tracker | label | Label of the tracker | addr | Bluetooth address of the tracker floorPlanId | | __`_id`__ of the floor plan of the position zoneId | | __`_id`__ of the zone of the position inside coordinates |x | X coordinate of the position with respect to the left side of the floor plan (meters) | y | Y coordinate of the position with respect to the bottom side of the floor plan (meters) stationary | since | Timestamp since the tracker has been stationary (UTC)
__NOTE:__ Multiple __`trackerId`__ can be specified (up to 100) using comma seperated query-string parameter value to filter multiple trackers. For example, __`?trackerId=5934c78bd3ffbc65ced4aeb9,5934c78bd3ffbc65ced4aeba`__ would return lastest positions of the two trackers with specified tracker ids.

*- Work in progress -* ## Map Markers Trackers' latest positions that are collected from [Web socket endpoint](#endpoint:9oRqxTX5XsLfvTp7W) may include `state` property. Currently, two states are exposed via web socket endpoint: `warning` and `alert`. If there is no `state` propery present, the tracker should be assumed to be in the `default` state. So, there is 3 states in total. Accordingly, trackers' map markers definitions may have up to **3 states** that can desribe the icon properties for various states. `default`, `warning` and `alert`. The `default` state marker defintion is a *required* field whereas `warning` and `alert` are *optional* and may be missing even when tracker's state is actually `warning` or `alert`. In these cases, `default` state marker properties are expected to be used as a backup. Map markers are based on [Leaflet.awesome-markers plugin v2.0](https://github.com/lvoogdt/Leaflet.awesome-markers). Available properties and default values are slightly modified and listed below. Further usage instructions can be found at the [Github repo](https://github.com/lvoogdt/Leaflet.awesome-markers).
**NOTE:** `marker` and `audit` property defintions are not part of default response. Should you require to access to `marker` property, it's required to use `_pull` query-string to retrieve these optional response parameters. For example, to retrieve `marker` property, `?_pull=marker` query-string is required to added to the request.
### Marker Properties | **Property** | **Description** | **Default Value** | **Possible values** | | --------------- | ---------------------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | | icon | Name of the icon | - | See glyphicons or font-awesome | | prefix | Selected icon library | `fa` | `fa` for font-awesome or `glyphicon` for bootstrap 3 | | markerColor | Color of the marker | `blue` | `red`, `darkred`, `orange`, `green`, `darkgreen`, `blue`, `purple`, `darkpuple`, `cadetblue` | | iconColor | Color of the icon | `#FFFFFF` | CSS hex color code | | spin | Make the icon spin | `false` | `true` or `false`. *(Font-awesome required)* | #### Supported icons The 'icon' property supports these strings: - `home` - `glass` - `flag` - `star` - `bookmark` - .... and many more, see: [Font Awsome Icons](http://fontawesome.io/icons/), [glyphicons](http://getbootstrap.com/components/#glyphicons) and [ionicons](http://ionicons.com) ---
__NOTE:__ Multiple `trackerId` can be specified using comma seperated query-string parameter value to filter multiple things. For example, `?trackerId=5934c78bd3ffbc65ced4aeb9,5934c78bd3ffbc65ced4aeb` a would return lastest positions of the two trackers with specified ids.

get.description:
Generates a secure WebSocket URL with expiration time for one-way communication between the clients and the backend. It's essentially MQTT over the WebSocket protocol to enable browser-based and remote applications to receive data from API backend in real time. Generated URLs expires in 4 hours as indicated with **`expires`** attribute in response object. You are expected to regenerate new urls when the generated URL expires should you choose to continue receiving real time data. You need to use a unique random string as **`clientId`** for connections.

Websocket connection must be established within five minutes after it is generated. Otherwise, the connection would be denied.

#### Example
Some MQTT clients, such as [Eclipse Paho for JavaScript](http://www.eclipse.org/paho/), support the WebSocket protocol natively. The following JavaScript code shows how to create a Paho MQTT client and call CONNECT to the backend. The **`url`** argument is the url collected from this [Generate WebSocket URL](endpoint:9oRqxTX5XsLfvTp7W) endpoint. The message broker uses the client ID to identify each client. Two clients with the same client ID are not allowed to be connected concurrently to the message broker. When a client connects to the message broker using a client ID that another client is using, a CONNACK message will be sent to both clients and the currently connected client will be disconnected.

```javascript
// Create a client instance
var client = new Paho.MQTT.Client(url, clientId);

// set callback handlers
client.onConnectionLost = onConnectionLost;
client.onMessageArrived = onMessageArrived;

// called when the client connects
function onConnect() {
  // Once a connection has been made, subsribe to a topic
  console.log("onConnect");
  client.subscribe(topic);
}

// connect the client
var connectOptions = {
    useSSL: true,
    timeout: 3,
    mqttVersion: 4,
    onSuccess: onConnect,
    onFailure: function() {
        // connect failed
    }
};
client.connect(connectOptions);

// called when the client loses its connection
function onConnectionLost(responseObject) {
  if (responseObject.errorCode !== 0) {
    console.log("onConnectionLost:"+responseObject.errorMessage);
  }
}

// called when a message arrives
function onMessageArrived(message) {
  console.log("onMessageArrived:"+message.payloadString);
}
```

After establishing a successful connection you can connect to a **`topic`** to receive real time information. Clients can subscribe to a topic using QoS 0 or QoS 1. MQTT QoS 2 is not supported.


## Real-Time Stream Topics Available
There are currently 10 types of topic available that streams real-time data. Responses are JSON objects. For topics, you need to replace **`<token>`** with the authentication token collected from [Generate Auth Token](#endpoint:QyMJkKihEmvxtntgy) endpoint. 

### 1. Tracker Positions

Streams latest positions in real time as they are received from the trackers. Once the client is subscribed to the topic, real-time tracker positions data stream will start.

#### Topic: `indoor/positions/latest/<token>`

#### Response Attributes:
__Parameter__ | | __Description__
--- | --- | ---
ts | | Timestamp of the position (UTC)
addr | | Address of the tracker. You can relate this address with trackers using the information collected from [List Trackers](endpoint:9LMH8kDxyjvQvWNa2) endpoint.
floorPlanId | | Id of the floor plan.
coordinates |x | X coordinate of the position.
 | y | Y coordinate of the position.
 
---

### 2. Tracker Events

Streams latest events in real time as they are received from the trackers. Once the client is subscribed to the topic, real-time tracker events data stream will start.

#### Topic: `indoor/events/latest/<token>`

#### Response Attributes:
__Parameter__ | __Description__
--- | ---
ts | Timestamp of the position (UTC)
addr | Address of the tracker. You can relate this address with trackers using the information collected from [List Trackers](endpoint:9LMH8kDxyjvQvWNa2) endpoint.
stationary | _(Allowed values: __`true`__ or __`false`__)_
 
---

### 3. Sensor Measurements

Streams latest sensor measurements in real-time as they are received from the sensors. Once the client is subscribed to the topic, real-time sensor measurements data stream will start.

#### Topic: `sensor/measurements/latest/<token>`

#### Response Attributes:
__Parameter__ | | __Description__
--- | --- | ---
ts | Timestamp of the position (UTC)
addr | Address of the sensor. You can relate this address with sensors using the information collected from [List Sensors](endpoint:7APHnCTkJGrd2xBjs) endpoint.
measurement | analog1 | Measurement from analog1 input. _(Optional)_
 | analog2 | Measurement from analog2 input. _(Optional)_
 | analog3 | Measurement from analog3 input. _(Optional)_
 | digital1 | Measurement from digital1 input. _(Optional, Allowed Values: 0, 1)_
 | digital2 | Measurement from digital2 input. _(Optional, Allowed Values: 0, 1)_
 | digital3 | Measurement from digital3 input. _(Optional, Allowed Values: 0, 1)_

---

### 4. Temperature Measurmenets

Streams latest sensor counter values in real-time as they are received from the sensor counters. Once the client is subscribed to the topic, real-time sensor counter data stream will start.

#### Topic: `temperature/measurements/latest/<token>`

#### Response Attributes:
__Parameter__ | __Description__
--- | ---
ts | Timestamp of the position (UTC)
addr | Address of the temperature sensor. You can relate this address with sensor counters using the information collected from [List Temperature Sensors](endpoint:72xSATiti8AHAxpyZ) endpoint.
temperature | Measurmenet from temperature sensor (°C)

---

### 5. Alarms

Streams alarm rule violations and recoveries in real time as they occur.

#### Topic: `alarms/latest/<token>`

#### Response Attributes:
__Parameter__ | __Description__
--- | ---
alarmRuleId | Id of the [Alarm Rule](endpoint:iZwWZsExgAQuHZNQk) that this alarm is associated with.
ts | Timestamp of the event (UTC)
eventType | Type of this event **`VIOLATION`** or **`RECOVERY`**
model | Model of the thing **`temperatureSensor`** or **`sensor`**
thingId | Id of the thing.
measurement | Latest measurement from the thing thas has triggered this event. (Object)
summary | Text summary of the alarm event.
